name: LEFT
description: LEFT returns the first character(s) from the beginning of a text string.
tldr: LEFT extracts a specified number of characters from the left side of a text string.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The text string from which to extract characters.

parameters.name: num_chars
parameters.description: Optional. The number of characters to extract (default is 1).

basicExample.explanation: Extracts the first 3 characters from "Hello World".

advancedExamples.title: Extract area code from phone number
advancedExamples.description: Get the first 3 digits from a phone number
advancedExamples.explanation: Extracts the area code from a phone number like "555-123-4567".

advancedExamples.title: Extract first word
advancedExamples.description: Get the first word from a sentence
advancedExamples.explanation: Combines LEFT with FIND to extract text before the first space.

howItWorks: LEFT counts from the beginning of the text string and returns the specified number of characters. If num_chars is omitted, it returns just the first character.

howToSteps.name: Select output cell
howToSteps.text: Choose where the result should appear.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The result shows the extracted text.

limitations: LEFT counts each character as 1, including spaces.
Use RIGHT to extract from the end, or MID to extract from the middle.

commonErrors.fix: Ensure num_chars is a positive number.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: LEFT works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: Does LEFT work with numbers?
faq.answer: Yes, numbers are treated as text. Use TEXT to format numbers first if needed.

faq.question: What if num_chars exceeds the text length?
faq.answer: LEFT returns the entire text string.
